author: Rocci J. Stucci
headline: A Mountain Fell on Wednesday Morning. Nepal Is Still Counting.
dek: A glacier collapsed above the Langtang valley and sent a wall of ice and rock down the Trishuli. Three days later, 676 are confirmed dead, nearly 3,000 are missing, and the lakes it left behind have not finished draining.
seoTitle: Nepal Floods: What We Know After the Langtang Collapse
seoDescription: A glacier fell above Langtang and took a valley with it. The Nepal floods have killed 676 and left nearly 3,000 missing. Here is everything we know so far.
seoKeywords: nepal floods, Langtang glacier collapse, Trishuli river, Rasuwa, Himalayan flood 2026
bulletPoints: A glacier near Langtang Lirung collapsed on Wednesday 26 August, touching off an ice-and-rock avalanche and a landslide that tore down the Trishuli corridor with no warning of any kind.
As of Saturday, at least 676 people are confirmed dead across Nepal and Tibet and nearly 3,000 are still missing, including more than 540 foreign nationals.
The Red Cross puts the number of people in urgent need at 93,000. UNICEF counts 17,000 children affected. More than 10,000 households need shelter tonight.
Nepal's finance minister estimates rebuilding at $4-5 billion, close to a tenth of the national economy, in a country that is still paying for the 2015 earthquake.
It is not over: two lakes formed by the debris are still draining, and there was no monitoring on that glacier because nobody had ever paid to put any there.
comparisonBody: This is being filed as a weather story, and it isn't one. There was no instrument on that glacier and no warning system in that valley — not because Nepal was careless, but because a country facing a $5 billion recovery bill cannot fund a Himalayan monitoring network out of its own pocket, and nobody else offered to. The other detail nobody is leading with: a community of 250 households swept away this week was made up of families resettled onto the Trishuli floodplain after the 2015 earthquake. They lost everything twice, eleven years apart, because the floodplain was the only flat ground on offer.
comparisonSourceLabel: Reuters: Nepal's flood damage may cost up to a tenth of economy to rebuild
socialNotes: Lead with the boy holding twenty rupees — that image is the whole piece. The 250-households detail is the credibility anchor and the argument: these are 2015 earthquake survivors who were resettled onto the floodplain.
